concepts.title: Agent harness
concepts.definition: The context, permission and environment Concorde gives one agent, derived from the Specs and the agent's task and applied through the agent program's own configuration.

concepts.title: Boundary
concepts.definition: The read and write limits one task receives, fixed by its task type and its bound Modules.

concepts.title: Boundary case
concepts.definition: One of the four explanations of a refused read, write or tool: overreaching work, a wrong project Spec, a Concorde implementation bug or a Concorde design limitation.

concepts.title: Boundary set
concepts.definition: One of the six sets the Protocol derives for a Module: its Spec context, external context, implementation context, Spec scope or implementation scope, or the project-wide ProjectImplementation shared by every Module.

concepts.title: Brief
concepts.definition: The prompt a worker receives: the Operation's task instructions followed by the grant's `rw`, `ro` and `names` lists as absolute paths and the rules of its boundary.

concepts.title: Brownfield workflow
concepts.definition: The workflow that describes a project whose code came before its Specs: survey, scaffold, code_to_spec per Module, spec review, task validation and delivery.

concepts.title: Build manifest
concepts.definition: The generated record of the digest of every source the build read and of every output it wrote.

concepts.title: Capability context
concepts.definition: The tools a worker may use and the contracts those tools reach, which tell it what it can do and never what the project promises.

concepts.title: Check result
concepts.definition: The record of one configured check run: the check, its Module, the status, the exit code, the digest of what was measured and the saved log with its digest.

concepts.title: Concorde defect
concepts.definition: A failure, wrong behaviour or design limitation of Concorde that would happen in any project using Concorde the same way, as opposed to a problem of the project it was seen in.

concepts.title: Concorde repository
concepts.definition: The independent Git repository of Concorde that a develop install is made and updated from, and in which the Concorde defects it reports are fixed.

concepts.title: Configured check
concepts.definition: A command that a Module's own checks file, `.concorde/checks/<module id>.json`, assigns to that Module, with its arguments, time limit and the input paths its result depends on.

concepts.title: Context
concepts.definition: Everything one worker may know: the union of its Spec context, external context, implementation context, capability context and task context.

concepts.title: Context identity
concepts.definition: The digest of the selected Spec sources and pinned external material together with the declarations that selected them.

concepts.title: Decision log
concepts.definition: The Markdown file next to a task record in which the session working on the task writes the choices it made without the developer, and to which escalations are appended.

concepts.title: Decision point
concepts.definition: A decision or open question in a run's output that the workflow treats as the developer's to settle: every open question, and every decision of a survey that the worker took rather than the developer.

concepts.title: Decomposition proposal
concepts.definition: The output of a survey: the child Modules to create with their purposes, bound entries and uses, the checks it proposes, the decisions it took and its open questions.

concepts.title: Defect report
concepts.definition: An Issue report the project's main agent writes about a Concorde defect, naming the project and Concorde commit it was seen on and carrying the whole error chain.

concepts.title: Delivery commit
concepts.definition: The commit Delivery creates on top of a workspace's branch it validated, holding the evidence bundle, the metadata its confirmations changed and every change not yet committed, and naming the workspace, the bundle and its readiness run in its trailers.

concepts.title: Deny rules
concepts.definition: The `permissions.deny` entries of the worker settings that forbid the file tools every path the grant does not make readable or writable.

concepts.title: Detached run
concepts.definition: A run whose runner the command starts as a process of its own, printing the run identity at once instead of waiting for the result.

concepts.title: Develop install
concepts.definition: An installation of Concorde into a project from the clean primary worktree of a Concorde repository the developer also changes, recorded as mode `develop` in the receipt and carrying Dogfooding's guidance.

concepts.title: Dogfood scenario
concepts.definition: A file naming a project, a fault, the developer's prompt and the expected outcome, under `scripts/e2e/scenarios/`.

concepts.title: Error chain
concepts.definition: The structured report of an error that travels up: one link per level that could not handle it, each with its detailed account and its reason for not handling it, and the errors it received from below nested as its causes.

concepts.title: Evidence
concepts.definition: A recorded check or review result, bound to the exact inputs it examined.

concepts.title: Evidence bundle
concepts.definition: The JSON file committed with a delivery that records the workspace, the readiness the delivery decided and the runs of the workspace that led to it.

concepts.title: Execution command
concepts.definition: A deterministic `concorde` command, such as `task-validation`, `delivery` or `scaffold`, that launches no worker and is run and recorded by the Execution runner exactly like an Operation.

concepts.title: Execution runner
concepts.definition: The deterministic process that runs one Operation's or execution command's steps in its workspace, launches workers only through the steps that ask for them and writes the run result.

concepts.title: External context
concepts.definition: The pinned documentation and source of external dependencies that the bound Modules' `external` inclusions select: the Protocol's ExternalContext of those Modules, read only.

concepts.title: File transaction
concepts.definition: A set of whole-file writes, each bound to the digest of the bytes it replaces, that is applied completely or, when a write or its final check fails while the process runs, not at all.

concepts.title: Grant
concepts.definition: The per-path access list, each path at level `names`, `ro` or `rw`, that one task type assigns to the bound Modules, computed from one worktree's Specs and identified by its context identity.

concepts.title: Headless session
concepts.definition: A `claude -p` or `pi -p` main session in a test project, run by the tool in one or more rounds and kept in a session directory.

concepts.title: History
concepts.definition: The folder `.concorde/history/` to which closing a task moves the task's whole folder, record, decision log and trace, where it is never changed and is only removed whole by retention.

contrasts.reason: the task record is the current state the task commands act on; the history keeps a closed task as it was

concepts.title: Impact index
concepts.definition: A derived reverse lookup that tells which Modules a change to a document, node, contract or file concerns.

concepts.title: Implementation context
concepts.definition: The code side of a worker's context: the names of the bound Modules' implementation files and, when the task type grants it, the contents of the whole project's code, the Protocol's ProjectImplementation.

concepts.title: Issue
concepts.definition: A durable, branch-local record of one concrete problem, holding every report made about it and its disposition history.

concepts.title: Issue report
concepts.definition: One immutable observation inside an Issue: what was seen, why it matters, the basis for the claim, evidence locations and who reported it.

concepts.title: Issue revision
concepts.definition: The digest of an Issue record's exact bytes, used to refuse a write over a record that changed after it was read.

concepts.title: Main agent
concepts.definition: The developer-facing Claude Code or pi session, started in the primary worktree, that discusses the project, splits work into tasks, hands every task to a task session and answers it, and merges the delivered tasks, asking the developer every question a task needs.

concepts.title: Main-session guidance
concepts.definition: The instructions, installed as a project skill for Claude Code and for pi and as a block of the project's `CLAUDE.md` and of an existing `AGENTS.md`, that tell the main agent how to work with Concorde.

concepts.title: Merge lock
concepts.definition: The lock of the primary worktree that one process at a time holds while it merges a task into the primary branch, opens a task or closes one; the kernel releases it when that process ends.

concepts.title: Module
concepts.definition: One cohesive responsibility of the software, with its own Spec; it need not be a package or directory.

concepts.title: Open question
concepts.definition: A behaviour the worker read but could not tell to be intended, reported with what it observed, why it is uncertain and the options, and written into no promise.

concepts.title: Operation
concepts.definition: A named job that combines host steps, service calls and one or more AI worker runs under Spec-derived grants, started with `concorde run` in a workspace, and returns exactly one run result.

concepts.title: Operation catalog
concepts.definition: The fixed list of Operations that gives, for each, its providing Module, its task type, the ids of its workers, whether it may run unbound, whether it may change the workspace and the contract of its output.

concepts.title: Permission extension
concepts.definition: The pi extension the Harness generates from a grant, which checks every file tool against it, runs every command in the sandbox and receives the worker result.

concepts.title: Progress file
concepts.definition: A worker run's `status.json` in its [run directory](#concept.run-directory), which the host keeps current while the worker runs so the main session can show what it is doing.

contrasts.reason: a worker run's progress file follows one worker; the run progress file follows the Operation or command run, which may launch several

concepts.title: Protocol binding
concepts.definition: The project configuration's explicit acceptance of one installed Spec Protocol copy, recorded as its version and the digest of its manifest.

concepts.title: Protocol copy
concepts.definition: The rendered Spec Protocol bundle placed in a project under `.concorde/protocol/`, whose manifest digest the project configuration binds.

concepts.title: Read-only check boundary
concepts.definition: The Linux sandbox in which a check runs: the whole host filesystem read-only, one fresh writable scratch directory, private process and IPC namespaces, and the host's network.

concepts.title: Readiness
concepts.definition: The outcome of Validation's readiness steps in one `task-validation` or `delivery` run: whether the workspace may be delivered, with its blocking findings, the checks run and the pending entries to confirm, bound to a digest of the exact inputs examined.

concepts.title: Registry
concepts.definition: The project-wide index of Modules, which mirrors every Module's `module` block and is never itself a place where relations are declared.

concepts.title: Resume round
concepts.definition: One continuation of the same worker session with the failures of the configured checks or, once they pass, with what the caller's own validation of the round reports to repair.

concepts.title: Review finding
concepts.definition: One problem a reviewer establishes in a reviewed Module's documents, with its location, dimension, severity, evidence and a suggested repair.

concepts.title: Review memory
concepts.definition: The findings the Spec reviews of one Module have kept, open or resolved, each under a stable id, tracked with the project so that a repeated review builds on them.

concepts.title: Review verdict
concepts.definition: The outcome of a Spec review or a Spec panel, derived by the Operation from the findings: `accepted`, `changes_required` or `incomplete`.

concepts.title: Run
concepts.definition: One execution of an Operation or an execution command in one worktree, with its own run identity, progress file and run result.

concepts.title: Run directory
concepts.definition: The [trace node](#concept.trace-node) `workers/<run-id>/` of one worker run, inside the node of the run that launched it, holding its run record, progress file, grant, brief, transcript and one node per round.

concepts.title: Run lock
concepts.definition: The file `locks/runs/<run-id>.lock` that a run's runner alone locks from before its first run progress file until after its result and removes as it exits, by which any observer tells, from any PID namespace, whether the run still runs.

contrasts.reason: the workspace lock keeps one workspace running one thing at a time; the run lock tells whether one run's runner still lives

concepts.title: Run progress file
concepts.definition: A run's `status.json` in its trace node, which the runner keeps current with what is running, where and in which step, and once finished with the status and summary.

concepts.title: Run record
concepts.definition: The host's durable record of one worker run, the `trace.json` of its [run directory](#concept.run-directory): its grant and context identity, settings, transcript, audits, checks, rounds and result.

concepts.title: Run result
concepts.definition: The structured envelope every run returns and saves: what ran, in which workspace, its status, its output, the worker's claims when there was a worker, the runner's own evidence and, when it is not ok, its error chain.

concepts.title: Run store
concepts.definition: Where Execution keeps its runs as [trace nodes](#concept.trace-node): `runs/` of a workspace folder, the step nodes of its workflow, and `.concorde/unbound/` of a worktree for unbound runs.

concepts.title: Run view
concepts.definition: The Concorde extension of a pi main session that starts Operations and execution commands in the background, shows every run and its worker's progress, and wakes the main agent when a run ends.

concepts.title: Runtime directory
concepts.definition: The private directory under `/tmp` that holds what one worker run needs only while it runs, its generated configuration, credential copies, home, temporary and working directories, and that the host removes when the run ends.

contrasts.reason: the run directory is the worker run's trace node and is kept; the runtime directory holds what the worker needs only while it runs and is removed

concepts.title: Session boundary
concepts.definition: The settings and write hook on Claude Code, or the boundary extension on pi, that confine a task session's file tools and shell to its task, leaving reads and the network open.

concepts.title: Session report
concepts.definition: The structured report with which a pi task session ends a session round: delivered with the delivery commit, or escalated with the escalations it recorded, plus its summary, decisions and open points.

concepts.title: Session round
concepts.definition: One headless run of a pi task session, from its prompt (the task at the start, or the main agent's answer) to its session report, a failure or a stop; a pi task session is a sequence of rounds on one pi session file.

concepts.title: Spec
concepts.definition: The documents in which a Module explains what it is for, how to use it, how it is designed and what it precisely promises.

concepts.title: Spec change
concepts.definition: The result of one specify run: the documents the worker changed, the documents the Operation created for it, the pending entries declared, the worker's account of the promises it changed, the Modules affected and the validation outcome.

concepts.title: Spec context
concepts.definition: The read-only documents the bound Modules' declarations select and the glossary entries of their terms: the Protocol's SpecContext of those Modules, which holds no external material.

concepts.title: Spec gap
concepts.definition: A promise that the stated goal relies on and that the Spec of a bound Module does not state, reported with where it belongs instead of being inferred.

concepts.title: Standard worker sequence
concepts.definition: The fixed sequence by which an Operation's step launches one worker: the step computes and freezes the grant and settles the worker's backend and model, and Workers prepares the settings and brief, launches the worker, audits it, runs checks with resume rounds and records the worker run.

concepts.title: Step agent
concepts.definition: The client-side relay of a workflow step: on Claude Code a small subagent that runs `concorde workflow step` once, waiting at most 100 seconds, while the step function asks again until the run has finished; on pi a command-runner agent that runs it once with `--stdin`, waiting until the run has finished.

concepts.title: Step key
concepts.definition: The name of a workflow step within its workspace, made of the name the script gives it and, when a restart label or answers are passed, that label and a digest of those answers.

concepts.title: Structural check
concepts.definition: One decidable rule of the Spec Protocol or of Concorde's Spec conventions, named by a rule identity and carrying the severity error or warning.

concepts.title: Task
concepts.definition: One unit of work of the main agent, made of a branch, a worktree checked out on it and bound as the workspace named after the task, a task record and a decision log.

concepts.title: Task context
concepts.definition: The material produced for one task, namely its brief, constraints and admitted artifacts, which adds no Spec or code source.

concepts.title: Task record
concepts.definition: The JSON file in the primary worktree that holds a task's identity, goal, Modules, branch, worktree path, base commit, stored state, escalated error chains, started task sessions and, once it ended, how it ended.

concepts.title: Task session
concepts.definition: A session of the main agent's own program to which the main agent delegates the work of one task, as it does for every task, working only inside that task's worktree until delivery and reporting to the main agent, to which it escalates together every decision the task needs that is not its own.

concepts.title: Task type
concepts.definition: One of the seven Protocol task types (understand, specify, implement, test, review-spec, review-code, code-to-spec) that fixes the access level of every boundary set a task receives.

concepts.title: Test project
concepts.definition: A codebase cloned at a pinned revision into the end-to-end root, from SWE-bench's repositories unless `--any` admits another, with Concorde installed, initialized and a task open.

concepts.title: Trace
concepts.definition: The tree of [trace nodes](#concept.trace-node) below one task or one unbound run, nested as the work was: a task's sessions, merges and workspace, the workspace's workflow and runs, each run's checks and worker runs, each worker run's rounds.

concepts.title: Trace node
concepts.definition: The folder one level of work leaves, holding its `trace.json` record in one uniform shape (identity, kind, times, status, own usage, error link, metadata, artifacts, references and its producer's content) with its files and the folders of the nodes below it.

concepts.title: Typed value
concepts.definition: A versioned JSON record `{type_id, schema_version, data}` whose data is checked against the schema its owner registered for that type.

concepts.title: Unbound checkout
concepts.definition: The throwaway detached checkout of the HEAD of the worktree an unbound run started in, made in a private temporary directory, in which the run's steps and workers work and which the runner removes before it writes the result.

concepts.title: Unbound run
concepts.definition: A run started in a worktree without a workspace binding, such as the primary worktree, which works in a throwaway detached checkout of that worktree's HEAD, records no workspace and may only read.

concepts.title: Verification declaration
concepts.definition: A statement in a test's own source that names the scenario identities the test verifies.

concepts.title: Worker
concepts.definition: One headless Claude Code or pi process that performs one bounded task of one task type under a frozen grant and reports only to the Operation run that launched it.

concepts.title: Worker backend
concepts.definition: The agent program a worker runs on, Claude Code or pi: the one the worktree's worker configuration chooses for the worker or its Operation, otherwise pi; both enforce the same grant.

concepts.title: Worker configuration
concepts.definition: A worktree's Git-tracked `.concorde/workers.json`, which gives a backend, a model and a reasoning level for every worker, for an Operation's workers and for one worker by its id, the most specific entry winning field by field, together with the limits of every worker launch and the runtime paths workers may read.

concepts.title: Worker id
concepts.definition: The stable name an Operation gives one worker it may launch, such as `spec_panel`'s `reviewer2` or `chair`, used alike in the worker configuration, the run record and the evidence.

concepts.title: Worker result
concepts.definition: The structured answer a worker ends with, validated against a fixed schema, reporting its status, a summary, its own error link when it could not finish, and the deletions it proposes.

concepts.title: Worker settings
concepts.definition: The Claude Code settings file the Harness generates from a grant, carrying the Bash sandbox, the deny rules and the write hook of one worker run.

concepts.title: Workflow
concepts.definition: A named procedure that orders the runs of one bound workspace and handles their results and decision points, written once and rendered for Claude Code and pi.

concepts.title: Workflow mode
concepts.definition: Whether a workflow run is interactive, ending at the first decision point or the first step that did not end ok so that its decisions are settled above the task, through the main agent, before it goes on, or no-ask, keeping every decision its workers took and reporting it at the end.

concepts.title: Workflow record
concepts.definition: The `trace.json` of a workspace's workflow [trace node](#concept.trace-node), in which Workflows records the workflow's name, every step with its run and node, and every report.

concepts.title: Workflow result
concepts.definition: The envelope `concorde workflow report` assembles from the workflow record and the saved run results: status, steps, decisions, open questions, deviations, pending decision points, problems and the error chain.

concepts.title: Workflow script
concepts.definition: The JavaScript source of one workflow's procedure, rendered by the build into a Claude Code workflow and a pi-subagents workflow script.

concepts.title: Workflow step
concepts.definition: One run of a workflow, of an Operation or an execution command, named by a step key and started and awaited through `concorde workflow step`, which returns the recorded run for a key it has seen before.

concepts.title: Workspace
concepts.definition: One worktree prepared for a bounded piece of work, with a name, a goal, the Modules it works on, the branch it works on and the commit it started from.

concepts.title: Workspace binding
concepts.definition: The file `.concorde/workspace.json` at a workspace's root that names it, its goal, Modules, branch and base commit, the workspace folder where its runs are traced and the `.concorde` whose `locks/` holds its locks, written by whoever prepares the workspace and only read by Execution.

concepts.title: Workspace lock
concepts.definition: The lock file `locks/workspaces/<workspace>.lock` of one workspace, held by the process running one of its runs for that run's whole life, so that a workspace runs one thing at a time.

concepts.title: Write audit
concepts.definition: The host's comparison, after each round and outside the worker, of the worktree's changes with the grant's `rw` list.

concepts.title: Write hook
concepts.definition: A small PreToolUse hook on Edit and Write that allows only the paths its policy names, a worker's grant's `rw` list or a task session's task worktree and decision log, and explains every denial.
